items.title: `infer_schema_length=None` not working as expected in multiple files reading
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

I have multiple jsonl files.
Some of the files have `key2`, while others don't.
#### File type 1
repeat following rows for >100 times in the file
```jsonl
{"key1": "value1", "key2": ["value2"]}
{"key1": "value1", "key2": ["value2"]}
{"key1": "value1", "key2": ["value2"]}
```
#### File type 2
repeat following rows for >100 times in the file
```jsonl
{"key1": "value1"}
{"key1": "value1"}
{"key1": "value1"}
```

I have around 1 jsonl files with `type 1` and 13 files with `type 2`.
```python
jsonl_files = [...] # the 14 jsonl files
result_df = pl.read_ndjson(
    jsonl_files,
    include_file_paths=include_file_paths,
    infer_schema_length=None,
)
```



### Log output

```shell
Sometimes, it would work fine, and `type 2` file column `key2` values are `null`.
But sometimes, it would raise Error:

  File "<path>/script.py", line XXX, in read_files
    pl.read_ndjson(
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        jsonl_files,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^
        include_file_paths=include_file_paths,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        infer_schema_length=5000,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "<path>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/polars/io/ndjson.py", line 174, in read_ndjson
    ).collect()
      ~~~~~~~^^
  File "<path>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/polars/_utils/deprecation.py", line 97, in wrapper
    return function(*args, **kwargs)
  File "<path>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/opt_flags.py", line 330, in wrapper
    return function(*args, **kwargs)
  File "<path>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/frame.py", line 2407, in collect
    return wrap_df(ldf.collect(engine, callback))
                   ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
polars.exceptions.ComputeError: expected dtype 'null' in JSON value, got dtype: Array
```

### Issue description

When files are short, the inferred schema are correct because it goes through all files.

When files are long, even when I set `infer_schema_length=None`, it might scan the whole file, but won't consider the cross-file differences.

### Expected behavior

It should always return without error. (For rows without `key 2` column, the value should be `None`)

items.title: `read_database` silently ignores `schema_overrides` for Arrow-based drivers
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import pyarrow as pa
from polars.io.database._cursor_proxies import ODBCCursorProxy # fake a driver without a real database


class FakeArrowOdbcProxy(ODBCCursorProxy):
    def __init__(self, values: list[int]) -> None:
        self._values = values

    def execute(self, query: str, **execute_options: object) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        pass

    def fetch_record_batches(self, batch_size: int = 10_000, *, fetch_all: bool = False):  # noqa: ARG002
        # arrow-odbc reports MSSQL TINYINT/SMALLINT as int32
        arr = pa.array(self._values, type=pa.int32())
        yield pa.RecordBatch.from_arrays([arr], names=["decision"])


values = [0, 1, 2, 3]
overrides: dict[str, pl.DataType] = {"decision": pl.UInt8()}

df_single = pl.read_database(
    query="SELECT decision FROM t",
    connection=FakeArrowOdbcProxy(values),
    schema_overrides=overrides,
)
print(df_single.schema) # Schema({'decision': Int32})
```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

`schema_overrides` is silently ignored when the driver returns Arrow data.
The column keeps the driver's type (`Int32`) instead of the requested `UInt8`.

Regression introduced in 1.43.2 by #28442, in `ConnectionExecutor._from_arrow`:

```diff
 frames = (
     self._apply_overrides(batch, (schema_overrides or {}))
     if isinstance(batch, DataFrame)
-    else from_arrow(batch, schema_overrides=schema_overrides)
+    else DataFrame(batch)
     for batch in self._fetch_arrow(...)
 )
```

`_fetch_arrow` always yields `pa.Table` / `pa.RecordBatch`, never a `DataFrame`,
so the `isinstance` branch never runs and schema_overrides is dropped entirely.
Works in `<= 1.43.1`, broken in `1.43.2`, `1.44.0` and `2.0.0-rc.1`.

### Expected behavior

`Schema({'decision': UInt8})`

The current workaround is an explicit `.cast(...)` after `read_database`.

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [10, 20, 30]})
print(df.select(pl.list(pl.lit(1), pl.col("x"))))
```

```shell
polars.exceptions.ShapeError: can't broadcast Series 'x' of length 3 to length 1

This error occurred in the following expression:
        dyn int: 1.as_list([col("x")])

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import io

# I'd expect the following two to give different results...
print(pl.read_json(io.StringIO('[{"a": "2020-01-01T12:34+05:00"}]'), schema={'a': pl.Datetime}))
print(pl.read_json(io.StringIO('[{"a": "2020-01-01T12:34+06:00"}]'), schema={'a': pl.Datetime}))

items.title: Datetime out-of-range in `group_by_dynamic` streaming engine
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import datetime

D = datetime.datetime
df = pl.LazyFrame(
    {"t": [D(2020, 1, 29, 23), D(2020, 2, 26), D(2020, 2, 29, 1)], "v": [1, 2, 4]}
)

# PanicException: slice index starts at 3 but ends at 2
try:
    out = df.group_by_dynamic("t", every="12h", period="1mo", include_boundaries=True).agg(
        pl.col("v").sum()
    ).collect()
except:
    print("failed")

# incorrect data
out = (
    df.group_by_dynamic("t", every="12h", period="1mo", include_boundaries=True)
    .agg(pl.col("t").alias("ts"))
    .collect(engine="streaming")
).row(1)

# second value is outside the window
print(out)


```


### Log output

```shell
# first issue (in-memory)
thread 'polars-1' (3579845) panicked at crates/polars-compute/src/rolling/sum.rs:143:31:
slice index starts at 3 but ends at 2
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
failed

# second issue (streaming):
(datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 30, 0, 0), datetime.datetime(2020, 2, 29, 0, 0), datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 30, 0, 0), [datetime.datetime(2020, 2, 26, 0, 0), datetime.datetime(2020, 2, 29, 1, 0)])
```

### Issue description

When dates get clamped, the (internal) monotonicity is affected. This results in failed queries (in-memory) or incorrect data (streaming engine).

### Expected behavior

Both queries succeed with correct results.

### Installed versions

reproduces on main and 1.44.1 as released

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Issue introduced by a new release

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import time
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

nrows = 10_000


def timeit(fn, label):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    fn()
    delta = time.perf_counter() - start
    print(label, f"{delta:.3f}s")


for ncols in (100, 1000, 10000):
    shape = (nrows, ncols)
    data = rng.standard_normal(shape, dtype=np.float32)
    data[rng.random(shape) < 0.05] = np.nan

    df = pl.from_numpy(data)

    df.select(pl.all().fill_nan(None))

    timeit(lambda: df.select(pl.all().fill_nan(None)), f"fill_nan {ncols} cols")
    timeit(lambda: df.select(pl.all().replace(float("nan"), None)), f"replace {ncols} cols")
    timeit(lambda: df.select(pl.first().fill_nan(None)), f"first fill_nan {ncols} cols")
    print()
```

items.title: In streaming mode, `.limit()` doesn't return early after join operations
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
from polars.io.plugins import register_io_source

N_BATCHES, BATCH = 50, 1000

def make_source(name, counter):
    def gen(with_columns=None, predicate=None, n_rows=None, batch_size=None):
        counter["n_rows"] = n_rows
        remaining = n_rows
        v = 0
        for _ in range(N_BATCHES):
            if remaining is not None and remaining <= 0:
                break
            n = BATCH if remaining is None else min(BATCH, remaining)
            df = pl.DataFrame({"k": range(v, v + n), name: [1] * n})
            counter["batches"] += 1
            if remaining is not None:
                remaining -= n
            v += n
            yield df
    schema = {"k": pl.Int64, name: pl.Int64}
    return register_io_source(gen, schema=schema, is_pure=True).set_sorted("k")

def run(label, join=True):
    lc, rc = {"batches": 0, "n_rows": "n/a"}, {"batches": 0, "n_rows": "n/a"}
    lf, rf = make_source("v_L", lc), make_source("v_R", rc)
    q = lf.join(rf, on="k", how="inner", maintain_order="left").limit(50) if join else lf.limit(50)
    out = q.collect(engine="streaming")
    print(f"{label}: out_rows={out.shape[0]} "
          f"L(batches={lc['batches']}, n_rows={lc['n_rows']}) "
          f"R(batches={rc['batches']}, n_rows={rc['n_rows']})")

run("control  bare source + limit(50)", join=False)
run("repro    sorted inner join + limit(50)", join=True)
```


### Log output

```shell
control  bare source + limit(50): out_rows=50 L(batches=1, n_rows=50) R(batches=0, n_rows=n/a)
repro    sorted inner join + limit(50): out_rows=50 L(batches=50, n_rows=None) R(batches=50, n_rows=None)
```

### Issue description

When doing a join between two lazyframes in streaming mode, and applying `limit()` to the output of that join, I would have expected that we stop fetching new morsels from the data sources as soon as the joined output has enough data.

Instead the `limit()` is ignored and all the data is loaded.



### Expected behavior

In the snippet I have custom io plugin data source; I run it once without joining and I get `n_rows=50` and only a single batch, which is the expected behaviour with `.limit(50)`.

Then I do a join between two identical datasources that have a sorted index, and the computation loaded all rows from the input data source (`n_rows=None`).

### Checks

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
from fastavro import reader as avro_reader


def read_with_fastavro(paths: list[Path]) -> list[dict]:
    records: list[dict] = []
    for path in paths:
        with path.open("rb") as f:
            records.extend(avro_reader(f))
    return records


df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "row_id": list(range(200)),
        "group": ["a" if i % 2 == 0 else "b" for i in range(200)],
        "name": [f"row_{i:04d}" for i in range(200)],
        "labels": [[f"label_{i}", f"label_{i+1}", f"label_{i+2}", f"label_{i+3}"] for i in range(200)],
    }
)

expected = df.to_dicts()

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
    paths: list[Path] = []
    for index, offset in enumerate(range(0, df.height, 50)):
        chunk = df.slice(offset, 50)
        path = Path(tmp_dir) / f"part-{index:05d}.avro"
        chunk.write_avro(path)
        paths.append(path)

    actual_polars = pl.concat([pl.read_avro(path) for path in paths]).to_dicts()
    actual_fastavro = read_with_fastavro(paths)

print(
    json.dumps(
        {
            "polars_version": pl.__version__,
            "expected_row_50": expected[50],
            "actual_polars_row_50": actual_polars[50],
            "actual_fastavro_row_50": actual_fastavro[50],
            "polars_matches": expected[50] == actual_polars[50],
            "fastavro_matches": expected[50] == actual_fastavro[50],
        },
        indent=2,
        ensure_ascii=False,
    )
)
```


### Log output

```shell
No additional output was emitted with POLARS_VERBOSE=1 for this reproduction.
```

### Issue description

Writing a single Avro file works correctly, but writing sliced DataFrames to multiple Avro files corrupts `list[str]` column values.

In the example above, row 50 keeps the scalar values (`row_id`, `group`, `name`) but its `labels` value is replaced with the value from row 0.

The same corrupted value is observed when reading the output with both:

- `polars.read_avro(...)`
- `fastavro.reader(...)`

So this appears to be a writer-side issue rather than a Polars Avro reader issue.

I originally found this while writing multiple Avro files from a production pipeline, but the reproduction above is independent of that application code.

### Expected behavior

Row 50 should remain unchanged after roundtripping through split Avro files.

Expected row 50:

```python
{
    "row_id": 50,
    "group": "a",
    "name": "row_0050",
    "labels": ["label_50", "label_51", "label_52", "label_53"],
}
```

Actual row 50:

```python
{
    "row_id": 50,
    "group": "a",
    "name": "row_0050",

### Issue description

The parquet file format has an `ENUM` logical type: https://parquet.apache.org/docs/file-format/types/logicaltypes/

> ENUM annotates the BYTE_ARRAY primitive type and indicates that the value was converted from an enumerated type in another data model (e.g. Thrift, Avro, Protobuf). Applications using a data model lacking a native enum type should interpret ENUM annotated field as a UTF-8 encoded string.

Polars currently doesn't use this type, but instead uses the logical `STRING` type when writing Enums to parquet files.
Additionally, and in my opinion the bigger problem is that, when reading a Parquet file with a logical `ENUM` type, such as for example a parquet file created by `parquet-java`, polars will read the column as `pl.Binary()`.  I guess it is impractical for polars to read the column as an `Enum` type, as there is no standardized way to encode the allowed options in the parquet metadata, but I believe that the column should instead be read as a `pl.String()` type. Both because the documentation specifies "Applications using a data model lacking a native enum type should interpret ENUM annotated field as a UTF-8 encoded string." and because polars only allows casts between String and Enum, not Binary and Enum. This means that loading a parquet file with enums requires two casts instead of just one:

```python
my_schema = {"color": pl.Enum(["RED", "GREEN", "BLUE"])}
df = (
    pl.scan_parquet("rgb.parquet")
    .cast({"color": pl.String()})
    .cast(my_schema)
)
```

### Expected behavior

Polars should read parquet columns with `ENUM` logical type as `pl.String()`, not `pl.Binary()` if it can't determine the allowed enum values from metadata.

Optional: Polars should use the `ENUM` logical type when writing `pl.Enum()` columns to parquet.

items.title: Rolling computes the wrong window when offset is not the negation of period (in-memory engine)
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
from datetime import datetime

import polars as pl


def rolling(ts, period, offset, time_zone=None):
    lf = pl.LazyFrame({"t": ts})
    if time_zone is not None:
        lf = lf.with_columns(pl.col("t").dt.replace_time_zone(time_zone))
    lf = lf.rolling(index_column="t", period=period, offset=offset).agg(pl.len())
    return lf.collect()["len"].to_list(), lf.collect(engine="streaming")["len"].to_list()


# Case 1 -- calendar month. offset="-1mo", period="28d".
# The window of the row at t is (t + offset, t + offset + period]:
#   2024-03-01 -> (2024-02-01, 2024-02-29]  -> 0
#   2024-03-31 -> (2024-02-29, 2024-03-28]  -> 1  (2024-03-01)
#   2024-04-01 -> (2024-03-01, 2024-03-29]  -> 0
mem, stream = rolling(
    [datetime(2024, 3, 1), datetime(2024, 3, 31), datetime(2024, 4, 1)], "28d", "-1mo"
)
print(f"month  in-memory={mem}  streaming={stream}  expected=[0, 1, 0]")

# Case 2 -- daylight saving. offset="-1d", period="24h", Europe/Amsterdam.
# Clocks go forward 2024-03-31 02:00 -> 03:00, so that calendar day is 23h long and
# 2024-03-31 00:00 + 24h lands at 2024-04-01 01:00. For t = 2024-04-01 00:00 the window is
#   (2024-03-31 00:00, 2024-04-01 01:00]
# which holds both 2024-04-01 00:00 and 2024-04-01 01:00 -> 2.
mem, stream = rolling(
    [datetime(2024, 3, 31), datetime(2024, 4, 1), datetime(2024, 4, 1, 1)],
    "24h",
    "-1d",
    time_zone="Europe/Amsterdam",
)
print(f"dst    in-memory={mem}  streaming={stream}  expected=[1, 2, 2]")
```


### Log output

```shell
month  in-memory=[1, 2, 2]  streaming=[0, 1, 0]  expected=[0, 1, 0]
dst    in-memory=[1, 1, 2]  streaming=[1, 2, 2]  expected=[1, 2, 2]
```

### Issue description

Report by an agent while implementing distributed rolling.

<details>

The in-memory engine gives the wrong window contents whenever offset and period are different durations that happen to share the same nanosecond estimate. The streaming engine is correct in both cases above.

The cause is a chain of three steps:

1. Duration::duration_ns() is an estimate — it scores a month as exactly 28 days and a day as exactly 86 400 s, so it is blind to both variable month length and DST.
2. group_by_values picks the fast lookbehind path on offset.duration_ns() == period.duration_ns(), using that approximate test to establish an exact property.
3. That path assumes t is the window's right edge and takes the shortcut let upper = t, whose own comment states the precondition it needs: "We have period == -offset". When the precondition does not actually hold, every window gets the wrong upper bound.

-1mo vs 28d and -1d vs 24h both satisfy step 2 without being inverses, which is why two unrelated-looking inputs fail the same way. The error direction depends on whether the calendar unit is longer or shorter than its estimate: the month case makes the window too wide (over-counts), the DST case too narrow (under-counts).

The guard inside the iterator is a debug_assert! restating the same approximate condition, so it cannot catch the misclassification even in debug builds. Two further branch conditions further down group_by_values compare duration_ns() the same way, so the shortcut branch is unlikely to be the only place this can misclassify.

Streaming is unaffected because RollingWindower tests the property structurally, if self.offset == -self.period, and otherwise derives the bound with real date arithmetic. Neg only flips the negative flag and keeps the fields, so that test correctly distinguishes -1mo from -28d.

Scope. Any in-memory rolling where offset is passed explicitly and is not the structural negation of period. The default offset=None becomes exactly -period, so ordinary usage is safe, and rolling_*_by is safe too since it builds offset by negating period. Note that #22980 would widen this, by making the shortcut reachable from rolling expressions as well.

Suggested fix. Use the structural test offset == -period for the branch condition, matching RollingWindower, and change the debug_assert! to that same condition so it becomes a real check.

</details>

### Expected behavior

In-memory engine behavior matches the correct streaming engine behavior.

### Reproducible example

This is an async program.  

```rust
use polars::prelude::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> eyre::Result<()> {
    let fname = "airports.parquet";
    let name = "CDG";

    let lf = LazyFrame::scan_parquet(fname.into(), Default::default())?
        .select([
            col("ident"),
            col("name"),
            col("latitude_deg"),
            col("longitude_deg"),
            col("elevation_ft"),
            col("iata_code"),
        ])
        .filter(
            col("iata_code")
                .eq(lit(name))
                .or(col("name").str().contains(lit(name), true))
                .or(col("ident").str().contains(lit(name), true)),
        )
        .filter(col("iata_code").is_not_null())
        .collect()?;
    dbg!(&lf);
    Ok(())
}
```
you need to fetch `https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/airports.csv` and convert it into parquet.

import polars as pl
df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]})

### Checks

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
# generate_mock_data.py
# script to mock a large df

import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from datetime import date, timedelta

np.random.seed(42)

n_rows = 100_000_000  # 100 million rows

start_date = date(2005, 1, 1)
end_date = date.today()
total_days = (end_date - start_date).days

date_offsets = np.random.randint(0, total_days + 1, size=n_rows)
dates = [start_date + timedelta(days=int(offset)) for offset in date_offsets]

range_weights = [0.4, 0.4, 0.2]
range_selections = np.random.choice(3, size=n_rows, p=range_weights)

shanghai_mask = range_selections == 0
shenzhen_mask = range_selections == 1
chinext_mask = range_selections == 2

codes = np.zeros(n_rows, dtype=np.int32)
codes[shanghai_mask] = np.random.randint(600000, 700000, size=shanghai_mask.sum())
codes[shenzhen_mask] = np.random.randint(0, 100000, size=shenzhen_mask.sum())
codes[chinext_mask] = np.random.randint(300000, 400000, size=chinext_mask.sum())

stock_codes = [f"{code:06d}" for code in codes]

factor_names = [f"ABCD2011_{i:04d}" for i in range(10)]
factor_name_list = np.random.choice(factor_names, size=n_rows).tolist()

factor_values = np.random.random(n_rows) * 100

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "date": dates,
        "id": stock_codes,
        "factor_name": factor_name_list,
        "factor_value": factor_values,
    }
)

df = df.with_columns(
    [
        pl.col("date").cast(pl.Date),
        pl.col("id").cast(pl.Utf8),
        pl.col("factor_name").cast(pl.Utf8),
        pl.col("factor_value").cast(pl.Float64),
    ]
)

df = df.sort(["factor_name", "date"])

df.write_parquet("mock_data/", partition_by=["factor_name", "date"])

df.write_parquet("mock_data.parquet")

df = df.sort(["factor_name", "date"])
df.lazy().sink_parquet(
    pl.PartitionBy("mock_data_sink/", key=["factor_name", "date"], include_key=False)
)
print("\nDone!")
print("Parquet files:")
print("  - mock_data/ (partitioned by [factor_name, date])")
print("  - mock_data.parquet (single non-partitioned file)")
print("  - mock_data_sink/ (sink partitioned by [factor_name, date])")

```

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
import os

os.environ['POLARS_ALLOW_NESTED_CSPE'] = '1'

buffer = io.BytesIO()
pl.DataFrame({"a": range(100), "b": range(100)}).write_parquet(buffer)

lf = pl.scan_parquet(buffer.getvalue())
inner = lf.select("a", "b")
outer = pl.concat([inner, inner])
q = pl.concat([outer.filter(pl.col("a") > 90), outer.filter(pl.col("a") < 5)])

# Both predicates must be pushed down all the way to the parquet scan.
# Currently, with POLARS_ALLOW_NESTED_CSPE=1, we only cache the unfiltered scan,
# which is why this is disabled by default (DEFAULT_ALLOW_NESTED_CSPE == false).
plan = q.explain()
assert plan.count('SELECTION: col("a") > 90') == 2, plan
assert plan.count('SELECTION: col("a") < 5') == 2, plan

assert_frame_equal(
    q.collect(),
    q.collect(optimizations=pl.QueryOptFlags(comm_subplan_elim=False)),
)
```

Adding the test to the repo in this PR https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/28857. Currently, it does not break, because `DEFAULT_ALLOW_NESTED_CSPE` is `false` by default. It will only break if we change this to `true`.

### Issue description

We only only cache the unfiltered scan and reuse it 4 times, see plan
```

      FILTER col("a") > 90
      FROM
        CACHE[id: ed4fc1ea-f18a-4d31-9f1f-f1abf7ddeb7f]

    PLAN 1:
      FILTER col("a") > 90
      FROM
        CACHE[id: ed4fc1ea-f18a-4d31-9f1f-f1abf7ddeb7f]
    PLAN 2:
      FILTER col("a") < 5

items.title: Data corruption when reading with cloud IO in concurrent write scenario
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

Difficult to reproduce, see description.


### Issue description

Reading files from cloud through `object_store` (e.g. `scan_parquet`) can result in data corruption if the file is also being written to concurrently. Since polars issues multiple, independent requests to the storage, requests might see different versions of the file. 

While GCS / AWS / Azure Blob Storage provide atomic writes (in the sense that a reader cannot see partial state), there's no built-in guarantee that independent subsequent requests see the same state. The way polars currently streams files, the requests *are* independent, and therefore subject to data races.

For example, a single `scan_parquet` might issue requests like this:

```text
HEAD              > size=1000, v1
GET [996..1000)   > v1 (footer len)
GET [900..1000)   > v1 (footer)
writer overwrites > v2 (size=1200)
GET [0..500)      > v2 (body)
GET [500..900)    > v2 (body)
```

### Expected behavior

I would expect polars to use the versioning mechanisms provided by the cloud stores to ensure data consistency within single read operations (e.g. `scan_parquet`).

labels.name: needs repro
labels.description: Bug does not yet have a reproducible example

items.body:
## Checks
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of Polars. (1.44.1)

---

## Reproducible example

The script writes 65 MB of Parquet data on its first run. The runner starts four
copies in one cgroup under sustained memory reclaim.

`repro.py`:

```python
import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import polars as pl

DATA = Path(os.environ.get("DATA", "data"))
ROWS, SHARDS, GROUPS = 12_000_000, 6, 20_000
WINDOWS = int(os.environ.get("WINDOWS", 24))


def generate() -> None:
    DATA.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for shard in range(SHARDS):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(shard)
        n = ROWS // SHARDS
        pl.DataFrame(
            {
                "g": pl.Series(rng.integers(0, GROUPS, n), dtype=pl.Int64),
                "k": pl.Series(rng.integers(0, 10, n), dtype=pl.Int64),
                "v": pl.Series(rng.integers(0, 10**6, n), dtype=pl.Int64),
            }
        ).with_columns(v=pl.when(pl.col("v") % 8 != 0).then("v")).write_parquet(
            DATA / f"{shard}.parquet", compression="zstd", compression_level=1
        )


def query() -> pl.LazyFrame:
    import pyarrow.dataset as pads

    files = sorted(str(p) for p in DATA.glob("*.parquet"))
    lf = pl.scan_pyarrow_dataset(
        pads.dataset(files, format="parquet").filter(pads.field("g") >= 0)
    )
    lf = lf.with_columns(seg=(pl.col("k") < 4).cum_sum().over("g"))
    key = ["g", "seg"]
    exprs = {f"c{i}": (pl.col("v") + i).cum_sum().over(key) for i in range(WINDOWS)}
    return lf.with_columns(**exprs).select("g", "seg", *exprs)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not list(DATA.glob("*.parquet")):
        generate()
    print(query().collect(engine="streaming").shape)
```

`run.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -u
export POLARS_MAX_THREADS=16   # Memory demand and the required watermark depend on this
python -c "import repro; repro.generate() if not list(repro.DATA.glob('*.parquet')) else None"
mkdir -p out; : > exits.txt
cat > .worker.sh <<'W'
#!/bin/bash
for i in 1 2 3; do python repro.py > out/s${1}_$i.out 2> out/s${1}_$i.err; echo $? >> exits.txt; done
W
chmod +x .worker.sh
systemd-run --user --scope --quiet \
  -p MemoryMax=13G -p MemoryHigh=12G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue \
  bash -c 'CG=/sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup | head -1)
           for s in 1 2 3 4; do ./.worker.sh $s & done; wait
           echo "$(cat $CG/memory.peak) $(grep ^high $CG/memory.events)" > .pressure'
echo "runs: $(wc -l < exits.txt)  failures: $(grep -cv '^0$' exits.txt)"
sort exits.txt | uniq -c
cat .pressure   # Lower MemoryHigh if the reclaim count is 0
```

Run `./run.sh`. Each query takes about a minute.

`MemoryHigh` triggers sustained reclaim without invoking the OOM killer. If the
`high` count in `memory.events` is 0, lower `MemoryHigh` until the count is nonzero.

## Log output

... (graph state updates continue until the process dies)
```

## Issue description

Under sustained memory reclaim, the query can segfault or return incorrect results.

### Segfaults

| Version | Failures |
|---|---|
| 1.44.1 (latest) | 5 / 12 |
| 1.41.2 | 19 / 48 across four trials, range 2-7 per 12 |

### Incorrect results

I compared completed runs with `engine="in-memory"` using the shape and each column's
sum and null count. Of 12 runs, 4 segfaulted, 4 were correct, and 4 returned incorrect
values. The incorrect results had the expected shape but differed in 1 to 3 window
columns. For example:

```
c23:  expected sum/nulls = [12110112893798, 1500341]
      returned             [11942075801291, 1429839]
```

Both the values and validity bitmaps differ.

With `debug-assertions = true` and `overflow-checks = true`, the process stops at:

```
Message:  unsafe precondition(s) violated: slice::from_raw_parts requires the
          pointer to be aligned and non-null, and the total size of the slice
          not to exceed `isize::MAX`
Location: crates/polars-utils/src/idx_vec.rs:281

polars_expr::dispatch::groups_dispatch::fw_bw_fill_null
  <Map<Zip<Copied<slice::Iter<u32>>, slice::Iter<UnitVec<u32>>>, _>>::next
  rayon::iter::...
```

The `UnitVec<IdxSize>` read from the grouped positions has an invalid pointer/length
pair when `as_ref()` constructs a slice. Less often, the same runs produce:

```
Message:  attempt to subtract with overflow
Location: crates/polars-arrow/src/bitmap/immutable.rs:752
  Column::split_at -> Series::split_at -> ChunkedArray<Int64Type>::split_at
    -> chunkops::split_at -> PrimitiveArray<i64>::split_at -> Bitmap::_split_at_unchecked
```

Here, `ubcc - count` underflows because the `Bitmap`'s cached unset-bit count is
smaller than the number of zeros in the subrange. In both cases, the structures have
inconsistent metadata when read. I have not identified its source.

### Conditions needed to reproduce

I tested each condition with 12 runs per variant and verified reclaim through
`memory.events`.

- Several distinct window expressions. With 24 expressions, 42-58% of runs failed.
  Fewer expressions required a lower `MemoryHigh` to reach reclaim.
- A low-cardinality, two-column key with many rows per group. About 42% of runs failed
  at 8 rows per group, compared with no failures at 1.7 rows per group.
- Nulls in the value column. Without a validity bitmap, the grouped paths return
  before reading the group index lists.
- `scan_pyarrow_dataset`. `scan_parquet` produced no failures in 12 runs. The Python
  scan disables common subplan elimination, leaving the window nodes in the plan.
- A wide result. Aggregating allows projection pushdown to remove the window
  expressions before reaching the failing path.
- 12 million rows. Tests with 4 million and 6 million rows produced no failures in
  12 runs under verified reclaim.

No specific thread count is required, but it affects memory demand and the required
`MemoryHigh` value.

#27842 also reports nondeterministic segfaults in the async executor on versions
1.37.1 through 1.41.2. Its stack trace is in work stealing rather than grouped
positions, so it may be unrelated.

## Expected behavior

Under memory pressure, the query should return the same results as an unconstrained
run or fail with a clear error. It should not segfault or return incorrect values.

items.title: .rolling(...).agg(...)  ~20–40x slower ≥ 64 threads
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import time

import polars as pl

# 250_000 rows: 1_000 groups x 250 rows. Group identity comes from the
# COMBINATION of 24 low-cardinality string keys (no single key is unique).
N_GROUPS, N_DATES, N_PAIRS, N_KEYS = 1_000, 250, 12, 24

idx = pl.int_range(0, N_GROUPS * N_DATES, eager=True)
g, d = idx // N_DATES, idx % N_DATES

data, keys, rem = {}, [], g
for i in range(N_KEYS):
    k = f"k{i}"
    keys.append(k)
    if i < N_KEYS - 1:
        card = 3 + (i % 6)
        data[k] = f"k{i}_" + (rem % card).cast(pl.String)
        rem = rem // card
    else:
        data[k] = f"k{i}_" + rem.cast(pl.String)

data["idx"] = d.cast(pl.Int64)
data["cnt"] = (((g + d) % 97) + 1).cast(pl.Int64)
for i in range(N_PAIRS):
    base = ((idx * (7919 + i * 13)) % 100003).cast(pl.Float64) / 1000.0
    data[f"m{i}"] = base - 50.0
    data[f"s{i}"] = (base % 17.0) + 0.5

df = pl.DataFrame(data)

# 24 aggregations: a count-weighted mean and stdev per column pair.
# The two families share the subexpression (cnt * m).sum() / cnt.sum().
exprs = []
for i in range(N_PAIRS):
    m, s, c = pl.col(f"m{i}"), pl.col(f"s{i}"), pl.col("cnt")
    exprs.append(((c * m).sum() / c.sum()).alias(f"wmean{i}"))
    tv = (c * (s**2 + m**2)).sum() / c.sum() - ((c * m).sum() / c.sum()) ** 2
    exprs.append(tv.sqrt().alias(f"wstd{i}"))

best = float("inf")
for _ in range(3):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    (
        df.lazy()
        .rolling(index_column="idx", period="753i", group_by=keys, closed="both")
        .agg(exprs)
        .collect()
    )
    best = min(best, time.perf_counter() - t0)

print(f"polars {pl.__version__}  threads={pl.thread_pool_size():3d}  best_of_3={best:.3f}s")


# for T in 32 63 64 120; do POLARS_MAX_THREADS=$T python repro.py; done
```


### Log output

```shell
polars 1.43.1  threads= 32  best_of_3=0.059s
polars 1.43.1  threads= 63  best_of_3=0.060s
polars 1.43.1  threads= 64  best_of_3=1.367s     <- 23x from one extra thread
polars 1.43.1  threads=120  best_of_3=2.230s

polars 1.34.0  threads= 63  best_of_3=0.062s
polars 1.34.0  threads= 64  best_of_3=0.062s     <- last good version: flat
polars 1.34.0  threads=120  best_of_3=0.072s
```

### Issue description

LazyFrame.rolling(index_column=..., period=..., group_by=...).agg(...) hits a hard performance cliff at exactly 64 threads: 60/61/62/63 are fast, 64/65+ are slow. The threshold does not line up with our socket boundary (60 cores/socket).

On 1.35.0 the same script at >= 64 threads panics instead:

```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at crates/polars-mem-engine/src/executors/group_by_rolling.rs:56:9:
internal error: entered unreachable code
```

1.35.1's fix for that panic (#25075, "Panic in group_by_dynamic with group_by and multiple chunks") appears to have replaced the panic with a fallback to a much slower path, and it has been that way through 1.43.1. 

Other observations that may help locate it:

The fast path needs "enough" keys + aggregations, and both expression families. With the 24 keys fixed: 20 aggregations take ~1.3s at any thread count (no cliff — the fast path never engages), 24 aggregations take 0.06s below 64 threads and 1.3s at 64+. Either family alone (24 weighted means, or 24 weighted stdevs, or 72 plain col.quantile()s) never engages the fast path and never shows a cliff. The two families share the subexpression (cnt * m).sum() / cnt.sum(), so this smells like agg-level CSE being enabled only under some width heuristic and disabled again when the pool is >= 64.

### Expected behavior

Thread pool sizes >= 64 should perform at least as well as 63 threads on the same query (as in 1.34.0 and earlier, which were flat from 32 -> 120 threads). One extra thread should never cost 20-40x.

items.title: scan_delta(DeltaTable) fails when DeltaTable uses delta-rs string storage_options (max_retries type mismatch)
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import polars as pl
from deltalake import DeltaTable
# delta-rs retry tuning (strings are required by delta-rs)
storage_options = {
    "connect_timeout": "30s",
    "timeout": "120s",
    "max_retries": "20",
    "retry_timeout": "600s",
    "backoff_config.init_backoff": "500ms",
    "backoff_config.max_backoff": "20s",
    "backoff_config.base": "2.0",
}
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    table_path = Path(tmp) / "delta_table"
    pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).write_delta(str(table_path))
    delta_table = DeltaTable(str(table_path), storage_options=storage_options)
    # delta-rs is happy with string options
    assert delta_table.version() == 0
    # Polars fails when reusing the same DeltaTable
    pl.scan_delta(delta_table).collect()
    # Workaround: override max_retries as int at scan time
    # pl.scan_delta(delta_table, storage_options={"max_retries": 20}).collect()
```

Note: passing ints directly in DeltaTable(..., storage_options=...) is not valid either — delta-rs rejects non-string values:

```python
DeltaTable(str(table_path), storage_options={"max_retries": 20})
# TypeError: argument 'storage_options': 'int' object is not an instance of 'str'
```

So consumers cannot satisfy both libraries with a single storage_options dict on DeltaTable.

### Log output

```shell
DeltaTable init: OK
scan_delta(DeltaTable): FAIL ValueError: invalid value for 'max_retries': '20' (expected int)
scan_delta(DeltaTable, override): OK
```

### Issue description

pl.scan_delta() accepts a deltalake.DeltaTable and merges table._storage_options into the parquet read path. When those options use delta-rs-style string values (which is required by delta-rs — storage_options must be dict[str, str]), Polars fails during collect() with a type error on max_retries.

This breaks the documented workflow of reusing a DeltaTable client (opened for writes/metadata) for lazy reads via pl.scan_delta(dt).

The same options work fine for delta-rs operations on the same DeltaTable (e.g. update_incremental(), write_delta(dt, mode="append")).

### Expected behavior

pl.scan_delta(delta_table) should work when delta_table was opened with valid delta-rs storage_options, including retry tuning keys documented for delta-rs/object_store (e.g. max_retries: "20").

### Installed versions

items.title: Datatypes have an inconsistent repr (not PEP 585-complaint?)
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

repr(pl.DataType) # DataType
repr(pl.DataType | str) # polars.datatypes.classes.DataType | str
```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

I use beartype to validate type hints in python. I have received the following error:

```plaintext
beartype.roar.BeartypeDecorHintPep604Exception: Type hint DataType inconsistent with respect to repr() strings: e.g.,
        >>> repr(DataType)
        DataType  # <-- this is fine
        >>> repr(DataType | int)
        polars.datatypes.classes.DataType | int  # <-- *THIS IS REALLY SUPER BAD*
    
        # Ideally, that output should instead resemble:
        >>> repr(DataType | int)
        DataType | int  # <-- what @beartype wants!
    
    Inconsistent type hints are unsupported by @beartype, which requires consistency between type hints and repr() strings. Consider reporting this issue to the third-party developers implementing this hint, which (probably) fails to define the PEP 585-compliant "__args__" and "__origin__" dunder attributes standardized by the "types.GenericAlias" API. See also:
        https://peps.python.org/pep-0585/#parameters-to-generics-are-available-at-runtime
```

I provided the copy of that example in the "Reproducible Example" field, as well.

This can be quickly fixed by modifying the repr to use the {module}.{qualname} formart like so

```py 
type(pl.DataType).__repr__ = lambda cls: f"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__qualname__}"

# Optional: Change the __module__ attribute so the repr is a much simplier "polars.DataType" instead of the full "polars.datatypes.classes.DataType".
# pl.DataType.__module__ = "polars"
# repr(pl.DataType) # 'polars.DataType'

# This of course would have to be applied to every datatype built into polars.
# repr(pl.Int32)        # 'polars.datatypes.classes.Int64'
```

### Expected behavior

Consistent repr no matter the usage.

```python
import polars as pl

repr(pl.DataType) # polars.datatypes.classes.DataType

items.title: Soundness: unchecked integer overflow in polars-arrow allows UB in safe Rust code
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://crates.io/crates/polars) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```rust
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
use polars_arrow::array::PrimitiveArray;

fn main() {
    let mut arr = PrimitiveArray::<i32>::from_vec(vec![1, 2, 3]);
    // offset=1, length=usize::MAX
    // assert!(1 + usize::MAX <= 3) → wraps to 0 in release mode → passes
    arr.slice(1, usize::MAX);
    println!("{:?}", arr); // heap-buffer-overflow: reads beyond allocated memory
}
```

Must be run in release mode (debug mode catches overflow automatically):
```
RUSTFLAGS="-Z sanitizer=address" cargo +nightly run --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

The same pattern exists in 13 `slice()`/`sliced()` implementations across polars-arrow array types. Additional overflow issues exist in `extend_from_lengths()` and `View::new_with_buffers()`.
Full list and regression tests in PR #27942.

### Log output

```shell
==1197527==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x6d7b50de001c
READ of size 4 at 0x6d7b50de001c thread T0
    #0 in polars_arrow::array::primitive::fmt::get_write_value::<i32, ...>

0x6d7b50de001c is located 0 bytes after 12-byte region [0x6d7b50de0010,0x6d7b50de001c)

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow in polars_arrow::array::primitive::fmt::get_write_value::<i32, ...>
```

### Issue description

Multiple `slice()` implementations check bounds with `assert!(offset + length <= self.len())`, which silently wraps
on overflow in release mode. This allows safe Rust code (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`) to trigger heap-buffer-overflow.

Per the Rust Reference:
> "if unsafe code can be misused by safe code to exhibit undefined behavior, it is unsound."
> — https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/behavior-considered-undefined.html

Affected locations: 12 array types + `Bitmap::sliced()` + `extend_from_lengths()` + `View::new_with_buffers()`

Note: Originally reported to security@polars.tech on April 22.
As these are soundness bugs (not externally exploitable), a public issue is appropriate.

Fix: PR #27942

### Expected behavior

`slice()` should panic on integer overflow instead of allowing undefined behavior.
Replacing `offset + length` with `checked_add` prevents the overflow.

### Installed versions

polars-arrow 0.54.4

items.title: Memory regression in 1.42.0: async Parquet prefetch count raised to 512 → ~2× peak RAM on streaming   scan_parquet → sink_parquet, OOMs scripts that worked on 1.41.2

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Issue introduced by a new release

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://crates.io/crates/polars) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

  Reproduction (self-contained; needs ~16 GB free to run the 1.42.x/32-thread case — lower ROWS/threads otherwise):

```
  import os, resource, sys
  import polars as pl

  DIR, OUT, FILES, ROWS, NCOL = "wide_parquet", "out.parquet", 32, 16_000_000, 89

  # A wide, highly-compressible table: ~200 MB on disk, several GB once decoded.
  os.makedirs(DIR, exist_ok=True)
  if len([f for f in os.listdir(DIR) if f.endswith(".parquet")]) < FILES:
      per = ROWS // FILES
      for f in range(FILES):
          idx = pl.int_range(f * per, f * per + per, dtype=pl.Int64)
          cols = {"id": idx.cast(pl.Utf8)}
          for k in range(45):
              cols[f"i{k}"] = pl.when(idx % 7 == 0).then(idx % 50).otherwise(None).cast(pl.Int64)
          for k in range(25):
              cols[f"s{k}"] = pl.when(idx % 5 == 0).then(pl.lit("c") + (idx % 12).cast(pl.Utf8)).otherwise(None)
          for k in range(NCOL - 1 - 45 - 25):
              cols[f"f{k}"] = (idx % 100).cast(pl.Float64)
          pl.select(**cols).write_parquet(f"{DIR}/{f:03}.parquet", row_group_size=50_000, compression="snappy")

  os.environ.setdefault("POLARS_FORCE_ASYNC", "1")  # automatic for cloud scans (s3://, gcs://, http://, ...)
  if os.path.exists(OUT):
      os.remove(OUT)
  pl.scan_parquet(f"{DIR}/*.parquet").sink_parquet(OUT)

  rss = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
  mb = rss / 1048576 if sys.platform == "darwin" else rss / 1024
  print(f"polars={pl.__version__} threads={os.environ.get('POLARS_MAX_THREADS','all')} "
        f"prefetch_size={os.environ.get('POLARS_ROW_GROUP_PREFETCH_SIZE','default')} peak_rss={mb:.0f}MB")
```

  Run:
```
  pip install "polars==1.41.2" && POLARS_MAX_THREADS=32 python repro.py     # ~8 GB
  pip install "polars==1.42.1" && POLARS_MAX_THREADS=32 python repro.py     # ~15 GB  (regression)
  POLARS_MAX_THREADS=32 POLARS_ROW_GROUP_PREFETCH_SIZE=64 python repro.py   # ~7 GB   (workaround)
```

  Workaround: set POLARS_ROW_GROUP_PREFETCH_SIZE back to ~`num_pipelines * 2`.

  Environment: 

### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

Upgrading 1.41.2 → 1.42.x roughly doubles peak memory for a plain streaming copy of a wide Parquet dataset read through the async reader (any cloud scan, or POLARS_FORCE_ASYNC=1 locally). On memory-limited machines this turns a job that completed on 1.41.2 into an OOM on 1.42.x, with no user code change.

  Root cause is the default row-group prefetch count. POLARS_VERBOSE=1 shows it jump from prefetch_limit: 64 (1.41.2) to prefetch_limit: 512 (1.42.x) at 32 threads. Each prefetched row group is decoded into memory, so 8× more concurrent decode ⇒ multiples more resident RAM. The accompanying prefetch_kbytes_limit byte budget does not bound this — setting it alone has no effect, because (per the code comment) it doesn't account for the decompression/decode expansion, and the count limit dominates. Peak RAM scales ~linearly with the prefetch count:

  polars 1.42.x, 16M rows × 89 cols, 32 threads:
    POLARS_ROW_GROUP_PREFETCH_SIZE = 8    → 2.9 GB
                                     16    → 3.8 GB
                                     32    → 5.3 GB
                                     64    → 7.0 GB   (≈ 1.41.2 default)
                                     default (512) → 14.9 GB

  Version comparison (same script, default settings):

                16 threads     32 threads
    1.41.2       4.8 GB          8.1 GB
    1.42.x       9.3 GB         14.9 GB     (~2×; OOMs a 16 GB host)

  We're aware of the // TODO: Dynamically adapt the max memory to the observed BDP next to this logic — but as shipped it's functioning as a bug: a fixed default of 512 concurrent prefetched row groups, chosen without regard to row-group width or available memory, is a silent ~2× memory regression on upgrade that breaks previously-working scripts. num_pipelines * 2 (1.41.2's behavior) was safe; a hard floor/target of 512 is not.

Relevant PR: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/27924


### Expected behavior

upgrading should not ~2× peak memory for the same streaming scan. The default prefetch count should scale with row-group width / available memory (or stay at the 1.41.2 num_pipelines * 2) rather than a fixed 512.

### Installed versions

polars 1.41.2 (good) vs 1.42.0/1.42.1 (regressed); Python 3.10; Linux/macOS; reproduces on the async reader path (cloud scans or POLARS_FORCE_ASYNC=1).

items.title: DataFrame `n_unique()` ignores additional columns when the `subset` parameter is an expression or selector that selects multiple columns
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({
    "id": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "A": [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2],
    "B": [1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 1,],
})

assert df.n_unique(subset=pl.col("A", "B")) == 5  # Fails, returns 4
assert df.n_unique(subset=cs.by_name("B", "A")) == 5  # Fails, returns 3
assert df.n_unique(subset=pl.exclude("id")) == 5  # Fails, returns 4
```

"id" -> 6 unique values
"A" -> 4 unique values
"B" -> 3 unique values
"A" & "B" together -> 5 unique rows

Columns "A" and "B" taken together have 5 unique rows. If the `subset` parameter of `n_unique()` is set to an expression or selector that selects both columns it should return 5. That doesn't happen. 

### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

If `subset` is set to an expression/selector that selects multiple columns, `n_unique()` considers only the first column and returns the number of unique values in the first column only, the additional columns selected by the expression/selector passed to `subset` are ignored. 

This issue also occurs when `subset` is set to a sequence that contains only one multi-column expression/selector.
```python
assert df.n_unique(subset=[cs.by_name("A", "B")]) == 5  # Fails, returns 4
assert df.n_unique(subset=[pl.col("B", "id")]) == 6  # Fails, returns 3
```
However, if the sequence has more than one element, the multi-column expressions/selectors in the sequence work fine, e.g.
```python
assert df.n_unique(subset=["A", pl.col("B", "id")]) == 6  # Passes
```

The DataFrame `unique()` method doesn't have these issues.
```python
assert len(df.unique(subset=pl.col("A", "B"))) == 5  # Passes
assert len(df.unique(subset=cs.by_name("B", "A"))) == 5  # Passes
assert len(df.unique(subset=pl.exclude("id"))) == 5  # Passes
assert len(df.unique(subset=[pl.col("A", "B")])) == 5  # Passes
```

### Expected behavior

If `subset` is set to an expression/selector that selects multiple columns, .e.g. `pl.exclude("some column")`, `n_unique()` should use all the selected columns jointly when determining the number of unique rows in the subset. Similarly, `n_unique()` should properly handle the case when `subset` is set to a sequence that consists of a single multi-column expression/selector.

items.title: `write_csv(quote_style="always")` writes nulls as `""`, silently turning them into empty strings on read
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import io
import polars as pl

buf = io.BytesIO()
pl.DataFrame({"s": ["a", None, ""]}).write_csv(buf, quote_style="always")
buf.getvalue()          # b'"s"\n"a"\n""\n""\n'     <- null and "" both written as ""
buf.seek(0)
pl.read_csv(buf)["s"].to_list()   # ['a', '', '']   <- null became ""```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

`necessary` and `non_numeric` write null as a fully empty **unquoted** field, distinct from the
quoted `""` used for empty strings — those round trips are lossless. `always` force-quotes null
fields too, which by CSV semantics *defines* them as empty strings, so null-ness is destroyed
for any reader including polars itself.

### Expected behavior

Null fields stay unquoted under `quote_style="always"`, as under the other styles: forced
quoting applies to values, and null is the absence of a value.

items.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

s = pl.Series([-9_223_372_036_854_775_808]).cast(pl.Datetime("us"))
print(s)
# pyo3_runtime.PanicException: invalid or out-of-range datetime
```

Investigating further, it's not just printing that fails, but further computation with the column also fails:

```python
result = s.dt.month()
# pyo3_runtime.PanicException: invalid or out-of-range datetime
```

The limit seems to be somewhere around `8_334_000_000_000_000_000` for microsecond datetimes:

```python
s = pl.Series("a", [-8_334_000_000_000_000_000]).cast(pl.Datetime("us"))
print(s)  # works, shows -262124-01-20 16:00:00
s = pl.Series("a", [-8_335_000_000_000_000_000]).cast(pl.Datetime("us"))
print(s)  # error
```

For nanosecond, it seems to underflow:

```python
s = pl.Series("a", [-9_223_372_036_854_775_808]).cast(pl.Datetime("ns"))

labels.description: Area: code that results in panic exceptions

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://crates.io/crates/polars) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```rust
use chrono::DateTime;
use polars::datatypes::{DatetimeChunked, TimeUnit};


fn main() {
    DatetimeChunked::from_naive_datetime(
        "datetime".into(),
        [
            DateTime::from_timestamp_nanos(i64::MIN).naive_utc(),
        ],
        TimeUnit::Nanoseconds,
    );
}
```


### Log output

```shell
thread 'main' (2638897) panicked at /Users/piyochan/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/polars-core-0.55.2/src/chunked_array/temporal/conversion.rs:39:14:
attempt to multiply with overflow
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

### Issue description

DatetimeChunked::from_naive_datetime panics when converting a NaiveDateTime whose nanosecond timestamp is outside the range representable by i64.  

Chrono had the same issue when converting DateTime values to nanosecond timestamps, and introduced DateTime::timestamp_nanos_opt() to handle values that cannot be represented as an i64 nanosecond timestamp.  
https://github.com/chronotope/chrono/issues/1289

### Expected behavior

successfully exit

### Installed versions

<details>

chrono = "0.4.44"
polars = "0.55.2"

</details>

items.title: Non-monotonic tz-aware temporal conversions keep a stale sorted flag, so `sort()`/`min()` return wrong results
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

**Part A — `dt.date()`**

```python
import datetime as dt

import polars as pl

utc = (
    pl.Series("t", [dt.datetime(2010, 3, 4, 13) + dt.timedelta(hours=h) for h in range(4)])
    .dt.replace_time_zone("UTC")
    .sort()
)
d = utc.dt.convert_time_zone("Antarctica/Casey").dt.date()

print("local times :", [str(x) for x in utc.dt.convert_time_zone("Antarctica/Casey").to_list()])
print("dt.date()   :", [str(x) for x in d.to_list()])
print("sorted flags:", {k: v for k, v in d.flags.items() if "SORT" in k})
print("min()       :", d.min(), " expected: 2010-03-04")
print("sort()      :", [str(x) for x in d.sort().to_list()])
print("expected    :", [str(x) for x in sorted(d.to_list())])
```

**Part B — `dt.truncate()`**

```python
import datetime as dt

import polars as pl

utc = (
    pl.Series("t", [dt.datetime(2014, 10, 25, 12) + dt.timedelta(hours=h) for h in range(4)])
    .dt.replace_time_zone("UTC")
    .sort()
)
loc = utc.dt.convert_time_zone("Asia/Magadan")
t = loc.dt.truncate("1h")

print("local       :", [str(x) for x in loc.to_list()])
print("dt.truncate :", [str(x) for x in t.to_list()])
print("sorted flags:", {k: v for k, v in t.flags.items() if "SORT" in k})
print("is_sorted() :", t.is_sorted(), " expected: False")
print("sort()      :", [str(x) for x in t.sort().to_list()])
print("expected    :", [str(x) for x in sorted(t.to_list())])
```

### Log output

```shell
local times : ['2010-03-05 00:00:00+11:00', '2010-03-05 01:00:00+11:00', '2010-03-04 23:00:00+08:00', '2010-03-05 00:00:00+08:00']
dt.date()   : ['2010-03-05', '2010-03-05', '2010-03-04', '2010-03-05']
sorted flags: {'SORTED_ASC': True, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
min()       : 2010-03-05  expected: 2010-03-04
sort()      : ['2010-03-05', '2010-03-05', '2010-03-04', '2010-03-05']
expected    : ['2010-03-04', '2010-03-05', '2010-03-05', '2010-03-05']


Part B:


local       : ['2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 00:00:00+10:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+10:00']
dt.truncate : ['2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00']
sorted flags: {'SORTED_ASC': True, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
is_sorted() : True  expected: False
sort()      : ['2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00']
expected    : ['2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 00:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00', '2014-10-26 01:00:00+12:00']
```

### Issue description

wo temporal kernels copy the input's sorted flag onto their output, but neither conversion is
monotonic for timezone-aware input. The resulting column is genuinely unsorted while reporting
`SORTED_ASC`, so `.sort()` becomes a no-op and `min()` can return a value that is not the minimum.

#### Part A — `dt.date()`

`crates/polars-expr/src/dispatch/datetime.rs:99-105` preserves the sorted flag through
`dt.date()` on a tz-aware Datetime, on the assumption that no timezone ever moves the local date
backwards:

```rust
// `replace_time_zone` may unset sorted flag. But, we're only taking the date
// part of the result, so we can safely preserve the sorted flag here. We may
// need to make an exception if a time zone introduces a change which involves
// "going back in time" and repeating a day, but we're not aware of that ever
// having happened.
out.set_sorted_flag(s.is_sorted_flag());
```

That assumption does not hold. Scanning every zone in the tz database hourly from 1890 to 2040
finds two offset changes where the local **date** goes backwards while UTC goes forwards:

```
America/Goose_Bay   UTC 1988-10-30 02:00 -> 03:00   local date 1988-10-30 -> 1988-10-29
Antarctica/Casey    UTC 2010-03-04 14:00 -> 15:00   local date 2010-03-05 -> 2010-03-04
```

Both are ordinary tzdata entries: Goose Bay ended DST at 00:01 local, stepping back to 23:01 the
previous day, and Casey moved from +11 to +08. So the resulting Date column is not sorted, but
claims to be — `min()` returns `2010-03-05` when the minimum is `2010-03-04`, and `.sort()`
returns the input unchanged. The `America/Goose_Bay` instant above gives a wrong `.sort()` too.

The scan that finds these is reproducible with:

```python
import datetime as dt, zoneinfo, polars as pl

hourly = (pl.datetime_range(dt.datetime(1890, 1, 1), dt.datetime(2040, 1, 1),
                            interval="1h", eager=True, time_unit="us")
          .dt.replace_time_zone("UTC"))
for tz in sorted(zoneinfo.available_timezones()):
    try:
        d = hourly.dt.convert_time_zone(tz).dt.date()
    except Exception:
        continue  # tzdata ships a few pseudo-zones polars rejects, e.g. 'Factory'
    if (d.cast(pl.Int32).diff().min() or 0) < 0:
        print(tz)
```

Severity for Part A alone is low, since it needs data spanning one of two historical instants, but
the comment is actively misleading for anyone working on this code later.

#### Part B — `dt.truncate()`

Same idiom at `crates/polars-expr/src/dispatch/datetime.rs:329`:

```rust
let mut out = match time_series.dtype() { /* ... truncate(tz, every) ... */ };
out.set_sorted_flag(time_series.is_sorted_flag());
```

Truncation is performed on the **local wall clock**, while the sorted flag refers to the
underlying **UTC** instants. When a zone changes offset, two ascending instants can truncate to
two descending ones. `Asia/Magadan` moved from +12 to +10 on 2014-10-26 (Russia leaving permanent
DST), so the local clock repeats `00:00, 01:00` and the truncated instants go backwards.

This half is more likely to be hit in practice — truncating a sorted timestamp column into hourly
buckets for resampling is routine, and Magadan/Chita are populated timezones, not research
stations. Scanning tzdata for 1970..2040 with `every` in `1h/30m/1d` finds 16 `(timezone, every)`
cases across 10 zones; widening `every` to also cover `1mo/1y/7d` gives 17 across 11 zones, and
extending back to 1890 gives 69 across 46 zones (including ordinary DST spring-forward
transitions such as `Canada/Newfoundland` 1988-04-03, where truncating into a non-existent local
hour shifts forward and breaks ordering).

Truncation on tz-naive input is monotone for all of those `every` values (0 violations over
hourly data 1890..2040), so tz-aware input is the whole of the problem:

```python
import datetime as dt, zoneinfo, polars as pl

hourly = (pl.datetime_range(dt.datetime(1970, 1, 1), dt.datetime(2040, 1, 1),
                            interval="1h", eager=True, time_unit="us")
          .dt.replace_time_zone("UTC"))
for tz in sorted(zoneinfo.available_timezones()):
    try:
        loc = hourly.dt.convert_time_zone(tz).sort()
    except Exception:
        continue  # tzdata ships pseudo-zones polars rejects, e.g. 'Factory'
    for every in ("1h", "30m", "1d"):
        try:
            t = loc.dt.truncate(every)
        except Exception:
            continue  # some zones have non-existent local times for a given `every`
        if t.flags.get("SORTED_ASC") and (t.cast(pl.Int64).diff().min() or 0) < 0:
            print(tz, every)
```

### Expected behavior

Part A: `min()` returns `2010-03-04` and `.sort()` returns
`['2010-03-04', '2010-03-05', '2010-03-05', '2010-03-05']`.

Part B: `is_sorted()` returns `False` and `.sort()` returns the four instants in ascending order.

In both cases the sorted flag should not be preserved for tz-aware input — only for tz-naive
input, where the conversion really is monotonic.

Platform:            macOS-26.5.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O

items.title: Inconsistent behavior when exporting to Arrow schema
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import csv
import tempfile
import polars as pl
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.csv

df = pl.DataFrame([{'name': 'James', 'age': 10}, {'name': 'Anne', 'age': 20}])

schema1 = pa.schema(df.schema.to_arrow())
schema2 = pa.schema(df.to_arrow().schema)

print(f'Schema 1: {schema1}')
print(f'Schema 2: {schema2}')

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', delete=True, delete_on_close=False) as tmp:
    w = csv.DictWriter(tmp, fieldnames=['name', 'age'])
    w.writeheader()
    w.writerows(df.to_dicts())
    tmp.close()

    with open(tmp.name, mode='rb') as csv_file:
        reader1 = pyarrow.csv.open_csv(csv_file, convert_options=pyarrow.csv.ConvertOptions(column_types=schema1))
        reader2 = pyarrow.csv.open_csv(csv_file, convert_options=pyarrow.csv.ConvertOptions(column_types=schema2))
```



### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

The code above demonstrates 2 ways to create an Arrow schema from a polars DataFrame. However, `schema1` has a data type of string_view for name while `schema2` has a data type of large_string. This can be problematic like in the example when trying to use pyarrow to read a CSV enforcing a schema with a string_view data type: "pyarrow.lib.ArrowNotImplementedError: CSV conversion to string_view is not supported". A data type of large_string does not trigger such errors.

### Expected behavior

I feel these 2 schema generation approaches should yield the same result, so either both string_view for name or large_string, but not 2 different data types that evidently behave differently.

items.title: Projection pushdown drops scalar reduction from cross-join RHS → silent N×N row expansion
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

lf = pl.LazyFrame({"symbol": ["A", "B", "C"], "v": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]})
median = lf.select(pl.col("v").median().alias("v_median"))  # scalar -> 1 row

# `v_median` is never selected -> projection pushdown drops the median reduction
out = lf.join(median, how="cross").select("symbol").collect()
print(out.height)  # expected 3
```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

#### Summary

A `how="cross"` join against a scalar-reducing subquery (`lf.select(col.median())`)
silently produces **N×N rows** instead of **N** whenever the reduced column is
not selected downstream. The cross join's RHS — which should reduce to a single
row — keeps the un-reduced base row count, so every left row is multiplied by
every right row. No panic, just an inflated wrong result.

Trigger (all required):

1. a cross join (`how="cross"`) whose RHS is a scalar-reducing `select`
   (`median`, `mean`, …),
2. the reduced column is dropped downstream (absent from the final `select`),
3. projection pushdown enabled.

Keeping the column (`...select("symbol", "v_median")`) returns the correct 3 rows.

#### Isolation

Disabling projection pushdown restores the correct result; the other passes do
not matter:

| `collect(...)` flag | height |
| --- | --- |
| default                                | 9 ❌ |
| `projection_pushdown=False`            | 3 ✅ |
| `comm_subplan_elim=False`              | 9 |
| `comm_subexpr_elim=False`              | 9 |
| `predicate_pushdown=False`             | 9 |

The optimized plan shows the RHS losing its reduction. Before `81df1409a3`
the RHS is `SELECT [col("v").median().alias("v_median")]` (1 row); after it the
median is gone and the RHS is an empty projection over the shared base cache
(N rows):

```
# 1.40.1 (correct, height 3)
CROSS JOIN:
  LEFT PLAN:  simple π 1/1 ["symbol"] / CACHE / DF               -> 3 rows
  RIGHT PLAN: SELECT [col("v").median().alias("v_median")]       -> 1 row
                simple π 1/1 ["v"] / CACHE / DF
  -> 3 x 1 = 3

# 1.43.2 (buggy, height 9)
CROSS JOIN:
  LEFT PLAN:  CACHE[id: a111e439…] / DF["symbol","v"]; PROJECT["symbol"]   -> 3 rows
  RIGHT PLAN: simple π 0/0 []                                              -> 3 rows
                CACHE[id: a111e439…]   # same cache as LEFT, median dropped
  -> 3 x 3 = 9
```

#### Bisect result

Introduced by the projection-pushdown rewrite

**`81df1409a3` — "refactor(rust): Refactored projection pushdown with cache handling (#27422)"**
(nameexhaustion, 2026-05-04)

| polars | result |
| --- | --- |
| ≤ 1.40.1 | ✅ 3 rows |
| ≥ 1.41.0 (incl. 1.43.2) | ❌ 9 rows |

### Expected behavior

`height == 3` — pruning the unused `v_median` should not un-reduce the
scalar subquery, and a cross join against a 1-row RHS should not multiply rows.

### Installed versions

<details>

polars 1.43.2 (correct on 1.40.1 and earlier)

</details>

items.title: Arrow table import not setting `fast_explode` on dataframe

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or an improvement of an existing feature

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import time
import polars as pl

tbl = pl.DataFrame({"c": [[i, i + 1, i + 2] for i in range(1_000_000)]}).to_arrow()

for label, s in [
    ("pl.Series   ", pl.Series("c", tbl["c"])),
    ("pl.DataFrame", pl.DataFrame(tbl)["c"]),
]:
    s.explode(empty_as_null=True, keep_nulls=True)  # warm up
    t = time.perf_counter()
    s.explode(empty_as_null=True, keep_nulls=True)
    print(
        f"{label}  FAST_EXPLODE={str(s.flags['FAST_EXPLODE']):5}  {(time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000:.2f} ms"
    )
```


### Log output

```shell
pl.Series     FAST_EXPLODE=True   0.75 ms
pl.DataFrame  FAST_EXPLODE=False  2.63 ms
```

### Issue description

On Arrow import, the `Series` constructor sets `fast_explode` (see also https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/28632), while the `DataFrame` constructor does not. This may lead to missed performance optimizations. The MRE is just a proofpoint. 

Scope to include evaluation of the flag on import data from storage (or not).


### Expected behavior

Fast-explode should be set on DataFrame similar to Series.

### Installed versions

Reproduces on 1.43.1.

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

CALLS: list[int] = []

def instrumented_scalar_udf(s: pl.Series) -> pl.Series:
    CALLS.append(len(s))
    return s * 2


def instrumented_list_udf(s: pl.Series) -> pl.Series:
    CALLS.append(len(s))
    return s

#%%

print("\n=== Case A (control): scalar UDF reused twice, no .list.eval() ===")
df_scalar = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
shared_scalar = pl.col("a").map_batches(instrumented_scalar_udf, return_dtype=pl.Int64)
CALLS.clear()
df_scalar.lazy().with_columns(x=shared_scalar + 1, y=shared_scalar + 2).collect()
print(f"UDF invocations for 2 usages: {CALLS}  (CSE correctly dedupes to ONE call)")

#%%

print("\n=== Case B (bug): List-returning UDF reused twice, through .list.eval() ===")
df_list = pl.DataFrame({"a": [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]]})
element = pl.element()
shared_list = pl.col("a").map_batches(instrumented_list_udf, return_dtype=pl.List(pl.Int64))
CALLS.clear()
df_list.lazy().with_columns(x=shared_list.list.eval(element + 1), y=shared_list.list.eval(element + 2)).collect()
print(f"UDF invocations for 2 usages: {CALLS}  (BUG: TWO calls -- not deduped)")

#%%

print("\n=== .explain(optimized=True): Case A shows a __POLARS_CSER__ node, Case B doesn't ===")
shared_scalar = pl.col("a").map_batches(instrumented_scalar_udf, return_dtype=pl.Int64)
shared_list = pl.col("a").map_batches(instrumented_list_udf, return_dtype=pl.List(pl.Int64))
print("\n--- Case A ---")
print(df_scalar.lazy().with_columns(x=shared_scalar + 1, y=shared_scalar + 2).explain(optimized=True))
print("\n--- Case B ---")
print(
    df_list.lazy()
    .with_columns(x=shared_list.list.eval(element + 1), y=shared_list.list.eval(element + 2))
    .explain(optimized=True)
)

```


### Log output

```shell
# === Case A (control): scalar UDF reused twice, no .list.eval() ===
# UDF invocations for 2 usages: [3]  (CSE correctly dedupes to ONE call)
#
# === Case B (bug): List-returning UDF reused twice, through .list.eval() ===
# UDF invocations for 2 usages: [2, 2]  (BUG: TWO calls -- not deduped)
#
# === .explain(optimized=True): Case A shows a __POLARS_CSER__ node, Case B doesn't ===
#
# --- Case A ---
# simple π 3/3 ["a", "x", "y"]
#    WITH_COLUMNS:
#    [(col("__POLARS_CSER_0xdae5f06214112af3") + 1).alias("x"), (col("__POLARS_CSER_0xdae5f06214112af3") + 2).alias("y")]
#      WITH_COLUMNS:
#      [col("a").python_udf().alias("__POLARS_CSER_0xdae5f06214112af3")]

#
# Note col("a").python_udf() appears TWICE, verbatim, in Case B's plan -- no CSER node at all,

Assume I have a list column `col` coming out of the output of a python UDF, then calling multiple `col.list.eval(...)` in the same `with_columns` will result in multiple re-computations of the list column.

This does not happen with non-list columns.

items.title: `cast(Struct{...}, strict=True)` to renamed fields silently nulls every value
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

s = pl.Series([{"a": 1, "b": 2}])
s.cast(pl.Struct({"x": pl.Int64, "y": pl.Int64}), strict=True)
# [{'x': None, 'y': None}]        <- no error, all data gone
```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

Struct casts map fields by name and fill unmatched target fields with nulls — unconditionally.
`strict=True` doesn't raise even when **zero** fields overlap, so a "rename via cast" silently
replaces the whole column with nulls. Baselines: every scalar strict cast that can't convert
raises, and a struct field **value** failure under strict raises
(`pl.Series([{"a": 300}]).cast(pl.Struct({"a": pl.Int8}), strict=True)` →
`InvalidOperationError`) — only the field-*name* mismatch path is silent. Root cause:
`crates/polars-core/src/chunked_array/struct_/mod.rs`, `cast_impl` (~line 250) — the
missing-field arm returns `Series::full_null(...)` without consulting `cast_options`.


### Expected behavior

Under `strict=True`, a missing source field errors (or at minimum when no field matches).
Null-filling can stay for non-strict casts.
