items.title: ComputeError reading Parquet files with VARIANT LogicalType (field_id=16) entire file unreadable
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
"""
Generates a minimal Parquet file with a VARIANT LogicalType annotation
by patching the Thrift-encoded footer metadata. PyArrow reads it fine;
Polars crashes.
"""
import struct
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
import polars as pl

# 1. Create a valid Parquet file with a struct<value: binary, metadata: binary> column
table = pa.table({
    "id": pa.array([1], type=pa.int32()),
    "variant_col": pa.array(
        [{"value": b"\x02\x01", "metadata": b"\x01\x00\x00"}],
        type=pa.struct([pa.field("value", pa.binary()), pa.field("metadata", pa.binary())]),
    ),
})
pq.write_table(table, "/tmp/variant_test.parquet")

# 2. Patch the footer to add VARIANT(specification_version=1) LogicalType
with open("/tmp/variant_test.parquet", "rb") as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

footer_len = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, len(data) - 8)[0]
footer_start = len(data) - 8 - footer_len

# Find the "variant_col" SchemaElement in the Thrift-encoded footer
name_bytes = b"variant_col"
name_encoded = bytes([len(name_bytes)]) + name_bytes
footer = data[footer_start : len(data) - 8]
pos = footer.find(name_encoded)
assert pos != -1, "Could not find variant_col in footer"

# Skip past the name field and any subsequent fields until the stop byte (0x00)
idx = pos + len(name_encoded)
while footer[idx] != 0x00:
    byte = footer[idx]
    type_id = byte & 0x0F
    idx += 1
    if type_id == 5:  # i32 zigzag varint
        while footer[idx] & 0x80:
            idx += 1
        idx += 1

# Insert LogicalType = VARIANT(specification_version=1) before the stop byte.
# Thrift compact protocol encoding:
#   0x5C = SchemaElement.logicalType field (delta=5 from field_id=2, type=struct)
#   0x0C = LogicalType union field_id=16 (VARIANT), long-form (delta>15), type=struct
#   0x20 = zigzag(16) = 32, the field ID
#   0x15 = VariantType.specification_version (delta=1, type=i32)
#   0x02 = zigzag(1) = 2, the value
#   0x00 = stop VariantType struct
#   0x00 = stop LogicalType struct
variant_bytes = bytes([0x5C, 0x0C, 0x20, 0x15, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00])
abs_insert = footer_start + idx
data[abs_insert:abs_insert] = variant_bytes

# Update footer length
struct.pack_into("<I", data, len(data) - 8, footer_len + len(variant_bytes))

with open("/tmp/variant_test.parquet", "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)

# 3. PyArrow reads the VARIANT annotation correctly:
pf = pq.ParquetFile("/tmp/variant_test.parquet")
print("PyArrow schema:")
print(pf.schema)

print("\nPyArrow read:")
print(pq.read_table("/tmp/variant_test.parquet").to_pandas())

# 4. Polars crashes on the entire file, even when selecting a non-VARIANT column:
print("\nPolars read (full file):")
pl.read_parquet("/tmp/variant_test.parquet")
```

Output:

```
PyArrow schema:
<pyarrow._parquet.ParquetSchema object at 0x...>
required group field_id=-1 schema {
  optional int32 field_id=-1 id;
  optional group field_id=-1 variant_col (Variant(1)) {
    optional binary field_id=-1 value;
    optional binary field_id=-1 metadata;
  }
}

PyArrow read:
   id                                        variant_col
0   1  {'value': b'\x02\x01', 'metadata': b'\x01\x00\...

Polars read (full file):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
polars.exceptions.ComputeError: parquet: File out of specification: LogicalType union has no variant set
```

Even `pl.scan_parquet(...).select("id").collect()` (a column with no VARIANT annotation) fails with the same error, because it happens during footer/metadata parsing before any column is materialized. `pl.read_parquet(..., use_pyarrow=True)` works fine.



### Log output

```shell
_init_credential_provider_builder(): credential_provider_init = None
async thread count: 14
blocking thread count: 512
sourcing parquet scan file schema from: '/tmp/variant_test.parquet'
ERROR: parquet: File out of specification: LogicalType union has no variant set
```

### Issue description

The [`read_logical_type()`](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/crates/polars-parquet/src/parquet/handwritten_thrift/file_metadata_thrift.rs) function in the hand-written Thrift decoder handles Thrift field IDs 1–15 of the `LogicalType` union (`STRING` through `FLOAT16`) but does **not** handle field IDs 16 (`VARIANT`), 17 (`GEOMETRY`), or 18 (`GEOGRAPHY`). When an unknown field ID is encountered, the `read_struct_fields!` macro correctly skips its bytes via the default arm, but `ret` is left as `None`, so the function returns an error instead of treating the annotation as absent:

```rust
ret.ok_or_else(|| ParquetError::oos("LogicalType union has no variant set"))
```

This violates the Parquet specification's forward-compatibility guarantee ([spec](https://parquet.apache.org/docs/file-format/versions/#compatibility-categories)):

> New logical types are considered forward compatible despite the loss of semantic meaning. Readers that do not recognize a logical type should still read the underlying physical representation rather than reject the file.

This is tracked cross-implementation in [apache/parquet-format#599](https://github.com/apache/parquet-format/issues/599), where Polars is listed as ❌ for both unknown types and VARIANT with "no exact issue/PR". The upstream `parquet` crate (arrow-rs) handles this correctly — its `LogicalType` enum includes `Variant`, `Geometry`, `Geography`, and a catch-all `_Unknown` variant. The analogous `ColumnOrder` union had the same "no variant set" failure mode and was fixed the same way in [#27893](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/27893) / [#27896](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/27896).

**Real-world context:** This affects Parquet files written by Databricks Runtime 18.1.x (`parquet-mr version 1.16.0-databricks-0001`), which sets the VARIANT LogicalType on columns backed by Spark's `VariantType`. We hit this on a real Delta table where one column has this annotation:

```
optional group field_id=-1 some_column (Variant(1)) {
    required binary field_id=-1 value;
    required binary field_id=-1 metadata;
}
```

The files are fully spec-compliant — PyArrow, DuckDB, and Spark all read them without issue. This makes the entire table unreadable via `pl.scan_parquet`/`pl.read_parquet`, regardless of which columns are selected, since the failure happens while parsing the footer.

**Suggested fix:** in `read_logical_type()`, return `Ok(ret)` (an `Option<LogicalType>`) instead of erroring via `ret.ok_or_else(...)` when no known variant matches — mirroring how [#27896](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/27896) handled the analogous `ColumnOrder` case. This treats any future/unknown LogicalType as "not set", which is exactly the forward-compatible behavior the spec requires. The single call site in `read_schema_element()` would need a small adjustment too, since `logical_type` there is already `Option<LogicalType>`:

```rust
10 => logical_type = read_logical_type(prot)?,  // was: Some(read_logical_type(prot)?)
```


### Expected behavior

Files with unknown/unsupported `LogicalType` annotations (VARIANT, GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY, or any future addition) should still be readable. The unrecognized annotation should be ignored, falling back to the physical type / `ConvertedType`, instead of failing the entire footer parse.

```python
# Expected: succeeds, `variant_col` materializes as its physical struct<binary, binary> representation
pl.read_parquet("/tmp/variant_test.parquet")
```

items.title: `.struct.field()` after `shuffle()` seems to produce incorrect results
items.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [1, 2, 3]})
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

Noticed while experimenting with https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/18233

Using a struct should keep each "row" intact when shuffling:

```python
df.select(pl.struct(pl.all()).shuffle())
# shape: (3, 1)
# ┌───────────┐
# │ a         │
# │ ---       │
# │ struct[2] │
# ╞═══════════╡
# │ {3,3}     │
# │ {1,1}     │
# │ {2,2}     │
# └───────────┘
```

Adding field extraction seems to break this:

```python
df.select(pl.struct(pl.all()).shuffle().struct.field("*"))
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ a   ┆ b   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 1   ┆ 3   │
# │ 2   ┆ 2   │
# │ 3   ┆ 1   │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

It should be equivalent to `unnest` in this case?

```python
df.select(pl.struct(pl.all()).shuffle()).unnest("a")
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ a   ┆ b   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 2   ┆ 2   │
# │ 3   ┆ 3   │
# │ 1   ┆ 1   │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Expected behavior

field extraction and unnest should produce the same result?

### Installed versions

<details>


items.title: Grouped streaming AsOf join uses a lot of memory when the right side has many group matches wrt the left side

labels.name: needs repro
labels.description: Bug does not yet have a reproducible example

items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python

import polars as pl

n_groups = 50_000
left_rows_per_group = 4
right_rows_per_group = 2000

left = pl.DataFrame({
    "group": [g for g in range(n_groups) for _ in range(left_rows_per_group)],
    "time": [t for _ in range(n_groups) for t in range(left_rows_per_group)],
}).sort("group", "time")

right = pl.DataFrame({
    "group": [g for g in range(n_groups) for _ in range(right_rows_per_group)],
    "time": [t for _ in range(n_groups) for t in range(right_rows_per_group)],
    "val": list(range(n_groups * right_rows_per_group)),
}).sort("group", "time")

out = left.lazy().join_asof(right.lazy(), on="time", by="group").collect(engine="streaming")
```

### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

In crates/polars-stream/src/nodes/joins/asof_join.rs, distrubute_work_task processes a left morsel as an single unit:

while need_more_right_side(&left_df, right_buffer, params)? && !right_done {
    // pull more right morsels into right buffer …
}

// … dispatch left_df + right_buffer, then prune_right_side(left_df, …)

need_more_right_side / prune_right_side key off the first/last group of the morsels needs right-side rows far down the right stream, so the loop keeps pulling right morsels until the buffer spans every group in the morsel. Nothing is pruned until dispatch, so the buffer never shrinks between groups.

### Expected behavior

Dispatch one by-group at a time. Slice the left morsel on group boundaries and run the existing strategy-aware need_more_right_side / prune_right_side / check_left_continuity helpers per group. This bound the right side buffer to a single group’s live range and works for all strategies.

In a local test on proprietary data, this took a process from ~500G -> ~20G peak and ran slight faster.

Happy to create a PR with the patch or can leave to someone more familiar with the code base.

### Installed versions

<details>

```
Replace this line with the output of pl.show_versions(). Leave the backticks in place.
```

</details>

### Reproducible example

Unfortunately I cannot reproduce it in single snippet

### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

We hit a rare deadlock in `sink_parquet` (~1 in 10k runs) in our Dagster jobs running on Kubernetes. Happens both writing to Azure Data Lake and to local
  `/tmp`, so it's not cloud-specific.

  When stuck, the main thread is parked in `polars_stream::execute::run_subgraph` waiting on `tokio::runtime::park::Inner::park`, while all 4 polars
  async-executor threads are parked on `parking_lot::Condvar` and all 4 rayon `polars-N` threads are idle. Nothing is doing any work — looks like a lost
  wakeup.

  Looks similar in symptom to #25762 (but that's `scan_parquet` on S3), and feels like it could be the same class of bug as the one fixed in #21916 (waker
  mismatch between tokio and the polars-async runtime). The sink_parquet pipeline does mix tokio tasks (file open) and polars-async tasks (writer/encoder),
  with the main thread awaiting polars-async JoinHandles via `ASYNC.block_in_place_on`.

  I couldn't reproduce locally on macOS (tried ~200k iterations with constrained threads), so it likely needs production-like conditions (Linux, cgroup

items.title: `pl.from_dicts(..., schema=has_enums, strict=True)` silently nulls invalid Enum values
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
def test_pl_from_dicts_fails_if_invalid_enum_value() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(pl.exceptions.SchemaError):
        df = pl.DataFrame(
            [
                {"id": 10, "status": "draft"},
                {"id": 10, "status": "archived"},
            ],
            schema={"id": pl.Int64, "status": pl.Enum(["draft", "published"])},
            # Implicitly, strict=True
        )
```



### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

`pl.from_dicts(..., schema=has_enums, strict=True)` silents nulls invalid Enum values.

In the example given, `df` simply replaced the invalid `"archived"` value with `Null`. This is a huge bug, and goes against the promise of Polars being extremely strict when `strict=True`.

Maybe related to #23152.

### Expected behavior

I would expect a `pl.exceptions.SchemaError` to get raised.

### Installed versions

I tested with the following Polars versions:

* polars==1.37.1
* polars==1.36.1
* polars==1.33.0

It seems that this issue goes quite a ways back.

items.title: `json_decode` parses invalid json
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
pl.Series(["1,2", "3"]).str.json_decode(dtype=pl.Int64)
```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

`json_decode` concatenates everything as a list and then parses that list. This can result in successful parses of invalid json that becomes valid when concatenating into a list.

Note the above example adds an extra element, but you can construct more perverse examples that preserve the count, and therefore also won't trigger length alignment issues as an expression:
```python
pl.Series(["[1],[2", "3]"]).str.json_decode(dtype=pl.List(pl.Int64))
```

It's also worth noting that schema detection does catch this, but only if the invalid element is in the schema infer range:
```python
pl.Series([*(f"[{v:d}]" for v in range(100)), "[1],[2", "3]"]).str.json_decode()
```

items.title: Polars expression context masks Python exceptions with keyword-only constructors
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl


class RequiresContext(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, response: object, body: object) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.response = response
        self.body = body


def raises_provider_error(series: pl.Series) -> pl.Series:
    raise RequiresContext("the provider rejected the request", response={}, body={})


pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).select(
    pl.col("x").map_batches(raises_provider_error, return_dtype=pl.Int64)
)
```

With Polars 1.39.0 and later:

```text
TypeError: RequiresContext.__init__() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments:
'response' and 'body'
```

Previously, on version 1.38.x:

```
RequiresContext: the provider rejected the request
```

### Log output

```shell
async thread count: 14
blocking thread count: 512
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "<string>", line 6, in <module>
  File "<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/dataframe/frame.py", line 10536, in select
    .collect(optimizations=QueryOptFlags._eager())
     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/_utils/deprecation.py", line 97, in wrapper
    return function(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/opt_flags.py", line 361, in wrapper
    return function(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/frame.py", line 2624, in collect
    return wrap_df(ldf.collect(engine, callback))
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/functions/lazy.py", line 1098, in __call__
    rv = self.function(slp, *args, **kwargs)
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<venv>/lib/python3.11/site-packages/polars/expr/expr.py", line 5051, in _wrap
    return function(sl[0], *args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "<string>", line 5, in raises_provider_error
TypeError: RequiresContext.__init__() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments: 'response' and 'body'
```

### Issue description

## Summary

When a Python callback raises an exception whose constructor requires keyword-only
arguments, Polars' expression-context error handling attempts to recreate that
exception with only its string message. This replaces the original exception with
an unrelated `TypeError`.

The behavior was introduced in Python Polars 1.39.0 by #26716 ("Add expression
context to errors"). Polars 1.38.1 propagates the original exception; 1.39.0 and
later raise the constructor error instead.

## Why this matters

This affects third-party SDK exceptions with structured state. For example,
OpenAI's `APIStatusError` subclasses require keyword-only `response` and `body`
arguments. A provider failure raised from `map_batches` is therefore reported as
the unrelated constructor error, obscuring the provider's actual status and
message.

## Likely implementation path

The expression-context code added by #26716 handles a `Python` error by obtaining
its class and constructing a new `PyErr` with a one-item positional tuple:

```rust
let cls = value.get_type();
let out = PyErr::from_type(cls, (msg,));
```

That assumption is not valid for Python exception classes with required
keyword-only constructor arguments.

### Expected behavior

The original `RequiresContext` exception should be propagated, with expression
context added without reconstructing the exception from only a message. A
fallback wrapper would be preferable to replacing the original provider error
with a constructor failure.

### Checks

### Reproducible example

Apologies, I am not allowed to share the file that exposed it.

The malformed struct can only originate from a reader (every in-process `StructArray` constructor validates), so it isn't buildable from the Python/Rust API. 
**However**, the identical panic is reproduced in **#27489**, via a fuzzed JSON blob through `polars_json::deserialize`. 

The panic is in `new`, not any single caller, so a parquet/IPC harness (#27488) with a mismatched child length should surface the `unnest` path too.


[`StructArray::new`](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/133a52633ba7b0dc08c70a2662abf5d7547df06f/crates/polars-arrow/src/array/struct_/mod.rs#L122) does `try_new(...).unwrap()`, so a `ComputeError` (dtype/child-length mismatch) becomes a panic instead of an `Err`. 
Callers can't use `?`; on a rayon worker thread it unwinds the whole computation.

Propagate the `ComputeError` from `new`, or route remaining callers (unnest included) through `try_new` as #27489 did.

items.title: `Series.is_sorted()` returns `True` for nulls-last series when `nulls_last=False`
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python

import polars as pl

s = pl.Series([3, 1, 2, None]).sort(nulls_last=True)
print("is_sorted(nulls_last=True):", s.is_sorted(nulls_last=True))
print("is_sorted(nulls_last=False):", s.is_sorted(nulls_last=False))


```


### Log output

```shell
is_sorted(nulls_last=True): True
is_sorted(nulls_last=False): True
```

### Issue description

`Series.is_sorted(nulls_last=False)` incorrectly returns `True` for a series produced by `sort(nulls_last=True)`.

The issue appears to come from the `is_sorted()` fast path relying on sorted metadata that records only ascending/descending direction, not null placement. In the ascending case, when `nulls_last=False` is requested, the fast path can return `True` immediately for a series marked `IsSorted::Ascending`, without checking whether nulls are actually at the front.

As a result, a series sorted ascending with nulls at the end can still be reported as sorted for the nulls-first case.

### Expected behavior

`s.is_sorted(nulls_last=False)` should return `False` for above example since nulls are at the end, not the start.

items.title: Streaming engine: `BinviewHashGrouper` panics `internal error: entered unreachable code` at `binview.rs:245` on a string-keyed `group_by` under concurrent load

labels.name: A-panic
labels.description: Area: code that results in panic exceptions

labels.name: needs repro
labels.description: Bug does not yet have a reproducible example

items.body:
## What happens

Under concurrent load, a `group_by` on **string** keys, run through the **streaming** engine, intermittently panics:

```
thread 'async-executor-11' panicked at crates/polars-expr/src/groups/binview.rs:245:13:
internal error: entered unreachable code
```

which surfaces in Python as:

```
pyo3_runtime.PanicException: internal error: entered unreachable code
  at pl.collect_all(...)  # engine resolved to "streaming"
```

`binview.rs:245` is the fallthrough of `BinviewHashGrouper::get_keys_in_group_order`, which matches the grouper's key-schema column-0 dtype and only handles the binview types:

```rust
match dt {
    DataType::Binary => self.finalize_keys::<[u8]>(...),
    DataType::String => self.finalize_keys::<str>(...),
    _ => unreachable!(),   // line 245
}
```

## This looks like a tricky race condition

The panicking `group_by` keys are two **`String`** columns. Column 0 is therefore `String`, so the type-correct plan hits the `String` arm and runs fine **in isolation, every time**. The `unreachable!()` only fires under **concurrent** streaming execution — i.e. a `BinviewHashGrouper` reaches `get_keys_in_group_order` with a key-schema whose column 0 is neither `Binary` nor `String`.

This suggests some kind of data race or state reuse in the streaming `group_by` path.

## Environment

- **polars 1.41.2** (stock, from PyPI/conda; `pl.__version__ == "1.41.2"`), Python 3.13, Linux aarch64, 32 cores.
- No `POLARS_*` env set. Engine is the default `"auto"`, which routes this plan to new-streaming (panic thread names are `async-executor-N`).

## The operation

The failing sub-plan builds a per-group time grid: a two-**string**-key `group_by(...).agg(datetime_ranges(...)).explode(...)`, asof-joined back onto a shared cached source, collected together with a sibling frame via `pl.collect_all([...])`. Reduced to a self-contained, synthetic form:

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import polars as pl

n_per = 300_000
t = pl.datetime_range(datetime(2025, 1, 1), datetime(2025, 1, 1, 0, 10),
                      timedelta(milliseconds=2), eager=True, time_zone="UTC")[:n_per]

src = (
    pl.concat([
        pl.DataFrame({"t": t, "k1": "a", "k2": g,
                      "val": pl.Series(range(len(t))).cast(pl.Float64)})
        for g in ("g0", "g1", "g2")
    ])
    .lazy()
    .sort("k2", "t")
)

grid = (
    src.group_by(["k1", "k2"])                 # <- two String keys -> BinviewHashGrouper
       .agg(
           pl.datetime_ranges(
               pl.col("t").min().dt.truncate("500ms"),
               pl.col("t").max().dt.truncate("500ms"),
               "500ms",
           ).alias("t")
       )
       .explode("t")
)

joined = grid.sort("t").join_asof(src.sort("t"), on="t")

# In our pipeline this runs via pl.collect_all([...]) with engine="auto" (-> streaming).
pl.collect_all([joined, src.select("t", "val")], engine="streaming")
```

## Reproducing it is difficult and non-deterministic

The panic occurs only under load and is not deterministic. It reproduces reliably only when this plan runs **concurrently with a diverse mix of other streaming queries** across many processes (e.g. when we run our full parallel test suite that includes ~1700 assorted queries across 16 worker processes — the failing `group_by` then panics essentially every time). We could not reduce it to a minimal standalone reproducer; all of the following stayed clean:

- The plan alone, looped, on an idle machine.
- The plan under full CPU saturation (busy-loop burners on every core), 40 iterations.
- 12 processes × 20 concurrent runs of the same plan (homogeneous concurrency).
- Replaying the exact serialized `LazyFrame`s (`LazyFrame.serialize()`) — single-process/48-thread, 14-process, and a focused 24-process hammer on just the grouper sub-plan — **50k+ executions**, both `engine="auto"` and `engine="streaming"`.
- The live plan (forced streaming) alongside 14 processes of *diverse synthetic* streaming churn (varied string group-bys / asof joins / `datetime_ranges`+explode).

Only the real, broad, diverse concurrent workload triggers it.

Happy to test a patched build or add instrumentation (e.g. dump the offending schema/dtype at the panic site) to provide any additional information.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({
```

items.title: A `dict` as `schema_overrides` is not respected in `read_csv`.
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

This correctly interprets string values using categories.
```python
>>> pl.read_csv(b'bybit', has_header=False, schema=pl.Schema([('exchange', pl.Categorical())]))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────┐
│ exchange │
│ ---      │
│ cat      │
╞══════════╡
│ bybit    │
└──────────┘
```
If I pass `pl.String` in the schema but use a `schema_overrides` which is a list, I still get the same result.

```python
>>> print(pl.read_csv(b'3', has_header=False, schema=pl.Schema([('exchange', pl.String())]), schema_overrides=[pl.Categorical()]))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────┐
│ exchange │
│ ---      │
│ cat      │
╞══════════╡
│ 3        │
└──────────┘
````

But if I use a `dict`, it no longer works.

```python
>>> pl.read_csv(b'3', has_header=False, schema=pl.Schema([('exchange', pl.String())]), schema_overrides=dict(exchange=pl.Categorical()))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────┐
│ exchange │
│ ---      │
│ str      │
╞══════════╡
│ 3        │
└──────────┘
```

It also does not work even when using the implicit column name `column_0`.
```python
>>> print(pl.read_csv(b'3', has_header=False, schema=pl.Schema([('exchange', pl.String())]), schema_overrides=dict(exchange=pl.Categorical())))
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────────┐
│ exchange │
│ ---      │
│ str      │
╞══════════╡
│ 3        │
└──────────┘
```

It does not seem related to categories, since something similar happens with ints, for example.

### Issue description

Passing a `dict` to `schema_overrides` inside `read_csv` does not work and does not apply the overrides.

### Expected behavior

The overrides should be applied, like when passing a list.

items.title: Type of schema_overrides in read_csv not compatible with the implementation
items.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
from collections import UserDict
from io import BytesIO

import polars as pl
from polars.datatypes import String

data = BytesIO(
    b"ID,Name,Birthday\n"
    b"1,Alice,1995-07-12\n"
    b"2,Bob,1990-09-20\n"
    b"3,Charlie,2002-03-08\n"
)
pl.read_csv(data, try_parse_dates=True, schema_overrides=UserDict(ID = String))
```


### Log output

```shell
TypeError: `schema_overrides` should be of type list or dict
```

### Issue description

According to the signature of `read_csv`, `schema_override` can be a `Mapping[str, PolarsDataType]`. 

`UserDict[str, PolarsDataType]` is a `Mapping[str, PolarsDataType]` but it is not accepted.

In python 3.15, there will be frozendict (which is a Mapping but not a dict). It won't be accepted either.

### Expected behavior

Mappings, not only dicts, should be accepted, as described by the function signature.

As a side note, the error message is also misleading: schema_overrides accepts any Sequence (e.g. a tuple) and not only lists.
